key_insight: The AI-CO OCT output was strongly associated with Humphrey visual field mean deviation and showed an approximately linear numerical relationship, but it is not interchangeable with perimetry.
clinical_relevance: In routine eye care, AI-CO may help complement structural and functional assessment, yet clinicians should avoid using its unitless score as a direct substitute for visual field MD.
method: 819 eyes from 424 patients with AI-CO and Humphrey 24-2F or 30-2 testing within 1 year
Used Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, Passing-Bablok regression, and CUSUM linearity testing
evidence_signal: AI-CO all correlated strongly with Humphrey MD in both test groups (r=0.836 and r=0.854), with linearity not rejected but average differences showing the AI score was lower than MD.
watch_item: The output is unitless and showed substantial eye-level variability, so real-world implementation should not treat it as interchangeable with standard automated perimetry.
paper_title: Real-World External Evaluation of an OCT Image Analysis System (AI-CO) in Relation to Humphrey Visual Field Mean Deviation
